lowest_minor.description: The lowest minor of its Product major that can use it (ADR 0098); 0 when absent. A project's configuration ignores it.

settings.description: The settings it sets, nested by key.

max_requests_per_minute.description: How many requests a Run admits in a minute at most, spaced evenly (GCRA), whatever its concurrency; none by default. An Operator policy cap bounds it even when unset, and a run already going takes a tightened cap at its next admission.

otlp.description: Whether an engine process also sends each new Audit log entry, the hash with it, as an OpenTelemetry event to the OTLP/HTTP collector `otlp.logs_endpoint` names: off by default, and nothing is sent while `otlp.logs_endpoint` is unset. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

retention.description: How long the user's Audit log keeps an entry, in milliseconds, such as 15552000000 for the six months the EU AI Act asks of high-risk deployers. Unset, the default, nothing is ever pruned. Set, each append first prunes the entries older than it from the log's beginning only, leaving an anchor entry that carries the last pruned hash, from which `audit verify` checks the rest, and a pruning record at the tail. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

block_resources.description: The resource kinds the Session's pages never load, failed as `BlockedByClient` by its interception before every navigation: any of `image`, `media`, `font` and `stylesheet`; none by default. The never-block list still loads a challenge's own. In `standard` and `stealth` the Run warns once per Session that the site can see the missing loads.

headless.description: Whether the Session's Chromium runs with no window: `true` by default. Headless or not, the site sees one browser's identity, with no `HeadlessChrome` token in its user agent.

service_workers.description: Whether a site's service workers run in the Session's pages: `allow` (the default on Chromium) runs them under the Session's interception, each worker's own requests passing the domain policy, the Filter lists and the Session's routes, never a page's routes; `block` makes `navigator.serviceWorker.register()` reject as on a failed fetch of the worker's script, `register` staying the browser's own function, so that every request of a page reaches its routes.

max_unused_age.description: How long a Pinned artifact no installed executable pins stays in the Browser cache unused before the clean-up deletes it, and how long an executable's entry counts as installed after it was last seen: 30 days. `null` turns the automatic clean-up off. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

interval.description: How often a live Run writes a Checkpoint where the engine keeps its Checkpoints, on the engine's clock; none by default locally.

channel.description: The OCI repository the daily channel is pulled from, `host[:port]/path`: Goodfetch's own on ghcr.io by default, or a mirror of it, which `clean_up.update = daily` makes the configured destination. Only Operator policy and user and project configuration set it: a Recipe's or a run's value is `setting_locked`.

fetch_timeout.description: How long fetching a version of the Clean-up rules from its sources may take at a Run's start or resume: past it, a Run holds to the newest version this machine has, and a `clean_up.version` it cannot fetch refuses the start. 30 s.

lists.description: The URL `clean_up.update = upstream` fetches each Filter list from, by list: `ads` (EasyList), `trackers` (EasyPrivacy), `annoyances` (Fanboy Annoyance) and `unbreak` (Brave's unbreak list); their authors' own URLs by default, or a mirror's. Each must be `https`. Only Operator policy and user and project configuration set it: a Recipe's or a run's value is `setting_locked`.

update.description: Where a new Run's Clean-up rules come from: `release` (the default), the set this release pins, with the embedded part as fallback; `daily`, the opt-in daily channel, whose registry it makes a configured destination, refused with `capability_unavailable` until the engine checks the channel's signature; `upstream`, the Filter lists from their authors' URLs, which it makes configured destinations. A Run holds to the version it starts with for its whole life, a resume included; `egress.offline` turns the fetching off. Operator policy can lock it.

version.description: The exact version of the Clean-up rules a new Run holds to, by its digest `sha256:<hex>` as Provenance names it, instead of the newest one `clean_up.update` gives: a daily version it names is fetched from the daily channel, and it is exempt from the channel's expiry and its refusal of older versions. None by default.

domains.description: The registrable domains on which a run accepts a consent wall, a Consent prompt with no refusal that covers the content or offers payment instead, rather than raising `blocked` with `consent_required`; `*` only when written. A prompt that offers a refusal is still refused there. A Recipe or a run only narrows it; it is widened only in an Operator policy, user or project configuration, or by a person's answer.

handling.description: Whether a browser Session answers Consent prompts: on by default in every Access mode, refusing each prompt in every frame and hiding one with no refusal that leaves the content readable. Off stops only the answering: the wall test still runs, and a consent wall is still `consent_required`.

on_wall.description: What a consent wall on a domain outside `consent.domains` does: `report` (the default) leaves the page at `consent_required`, raised as `blocked`; `ask` raises a Human pause for a person's answer, for this run or always for the domain. Until the Human pause takes a person's answer, `ask` opens no page: `capability_unavailable`.

address.description: Where the Daemon serves the Console, as `host:port`: `127.0.0.1` on port 7800 plus the major (7700 plus the minor during `0.y` previews), so each major's Console has its own port. Port 0 takes a free port, which the Daemon's runtime file and `daemon status` report. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only. An Attached engine serves no Console unless the script that starts it asks for one at an address of its own, which `hello` answers with the Console's sign-in link.

content_address.description: Where the Daemon serves the Console's content origin, which shows scraped HTML, screenshots, DOM snapshots and page bodies, as `host:port`. None by default: the Console's host on a free port, or, when `console.content_public_url` is set, the Console's own listener, which tells the two origins apart by the `Host` each request names. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

content_public_url.description: The origin a browser reaches the Console's content origin at behind a proxy, such as `https://content.example.com`, which the addresses the Console signs name. None by default: the content origin's own listener. With no `console.content_address`, the content origin shares the Console's listener and answers the requests that name this origin's host. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

offline_cache.description: Whether the Console keeps run summaries and their metadata in the browser, so that a page goes on showing them while it has no connection to the Daemon: `true`. The cache is encrypted under a key that only the sign-in's cookie unwraps, holds no secret field, and is wiped at sign-out; `false` writes nothing and wipes what an earlier page wrote. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

public_url.description: The address links to the Console name, such as `https://console.example.com`: the links in Notifications and a run's `console_url`. None by default: the Console's own address. A link never carries a token or a cookie, so a forwarded one grants nothing. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

idle_expiry.description: How long a Console sign-in lasts without being used, in milliseconds: 30 days. Each use starts it again; a sign-in unused for longer ends, and its person signs in again. Set in an Operator policy only.

rate.description: How many times one address may try to sign in to the Console in a minute: 10. A further attempt in that minute is refused, whatever its credential. Set in an Operator policy only.

extractor.description: The main-content step `page.formats` reads a page's main content with, before its Markdown, its main HTML and its text: `dom_smoothie` (the default), Readability's algorithm, or `trafilatura`, the rs-trafilatura port. A step that finds no text in a document holding text outside its navigation landmarks answers that text. Set at any scope down to a page: a Run, a Session's or a page's own `settings`.

content_types.description: The media types a Label's handler takes, each `type/subtype`, `type/*` or `*/*`, set for the Run or for one of its Labels, whose own list wins for its requests: `text/html` and `application/xhtml+xml` by default. A response that would reach the handler (a 2xx, or a status `crawl.handle_statuses` lists) of another type ends its request `skipped` with the reason `content_type` before its body is read, never retried. The type is the response's `Content-Type` essence, or, when it names none, the type the pinned Chromium's MIME sniffer gives its first 1,024 bytes; a response with neither a type nor a body is an empty HTML document. An accepted type that is not HTML or XHTML reaches the handler with its body in its response and a page holding no document, whose document calls fail with `response_not_document`. A handler's own navigations are not checked. A value that is no list of media ranges is refused with `setting_invalid` when the crawl starts.

domain_keys.description: Host names, each with the domain key its requests and those of the hosts under it share, the longest name winning, in place of the registrable domain under the Public Suffix List: a Recipe's override of the key its per-domain queues use. None by default.

handle_statuses.description: Statuses whose responses go to the handler as they are: a redirect status listed here is not followed, and the handler gets the 3xx as its response. None by default.

concurrency.description: How many work items the program's handler is given at once: 16, Scrapy's `CONCURRENT_REQUESTS`. A run already going takes a tightened Operator policy cap at its next admission.

keep_alive.description: Whether a crawl's Run stays `running` with an empty Frontier and nothing in flight, waiting for new work, until `run.finish` lets it end once its work items are done: `false`, so a crawl finishes once its work items are done. Its idle time counts toward `timeout.run`, and an abort stops it as any Run.

keep_url_fragment.description: Whether a crawl request's identity keeps its URL's fragment, so a hash-routed app's views (`#/a`, `#/b`) are separate requests, set for the Run or for one of its Labels, whose own value wins for its requests (Crawlee's `keepUrlFragment`). Off by default: one URL with two fragments is one request. Only the tiers that run the page's scripts serve such a request: under `fetch.tier: auto` it runs on `browser`, and forcing `http`, `browser_fetch` or `discovered_api` where it is on fails the crawl's start with `setting_not_applicable`. Fixed for a Run's life: a start under the Run's ID that changes it is refused with `setting_not_applicable`.

max_depth.description: How deep a crawl goes, its seeds at depth 0 and each enqueue one level deeper than the request whose attempt added it: a deeper request is not added, with `max_depth`, and a Run that refused one ends `incomplete`. None by default; `null` clears it.

max_path_segments.description: The most segments a URL's path may have, as the WHATWG parser splits it, an empty last segment (a trailing slash) not counted (Heritrix's `maxPathDepth`): a URL with more is not added, with `max_path_segments`, and a finished Run that refused one is `unverified`. 20 by default; `null` turns the cap off.

max_requests.description: How many requests a crawl admits, its seeds included: once it admitted this many, a further one is not added, with `max_requests`, and a Run that refused one ends `incomplete`. None by default; `null` clears it.

max_segment_repeats.description: How many times back to back a segment of a URL's path, or a run of segments, may appear (Heritrix's `maxRepetitions`), so `/a/a` passes and `/a/a/a` and `/a/b/a/b/a/b` do not, while numbers that recur apart, as in `/page/1/tag/1/sort/1`, do: a URL past it is not added, with `max_segment_repeats`, and a finished Run that refused one is `unverified`. 2 by default; `null` turns the cap off.

max_staged_enqueues.description: How many admissions one attempt may stage before it commits: its enqueues, `enqueueLinks` calls and seeds added through `ctx.run`, each held in the engine's memory with the attempt until its commit or its discard. One more fails with `staging_full`, and nothing is staged. 10,000 by default.

max_url_length.description: The longest URL a crawl admits, in characters as the WHATWG parser serializes it, without its fragment (Scrapy's `URLLENGTH_LIMIT`): a longer one is not added, with `max_url_length`, and a finished Run that refused one is `unverified`. 2,083 by default; `null` turns the cap off.

path_budgets.description: Budgets for sections of a site, each a table of `pattern`, a glob read as Playwright reads one and matched in the engine against a URL's path and query, such as `/shop?*`, and `max_requests`: the first entry whose pattern a request's URL matches counts it, and once that entry counted `max_requests`, a further request it matches first is not added, with `path_budget`, and a Run that refused one ends `incomplete`, its reasons naming the pattern and the count. A later entry the URL also matches does not count it. None by default.

max_requests.description: How many requests whose URL the pattern matches first the crawl admits.

pattern.description: A glob read as Playwright reads one, such as `/shop?*`, matched in the engine against a URL's path and query.

max_size.description: The longest a crawl request's Payload may be, in bytes of its JSON as the engine writes it, compactly: a longer one is refused at its enqueue with `payload_invalid`, whose `limit` names this setting, since a Payload lives in the Frontier and in every Checkpoint. Large content goes to the Key-value store, and the Payload carries its key. 64 KiB (65,536 bytes) by default.

handler_failed.description: Whether a work item whose handler failed with `handler_failed` is tried again: `false`.

max.description: How many times a work item whose attempt failed retryably is tried again: 2, Scrapy's `RETRY_TIMES`. A run already going takes a tightened Operator policy cap before its next retry.

sample_pages.description: How many pages the sample crawl visits.

exclude.description: URL patterns, each a glob read as Playwright reads one and matched in the engine, none of which a link may match, besides `crawl.scope.strategy` and `crawl.scope.include`. None by default. Fixed for a Run's life.

include.description: URL patterns, each a glob read as Playwright reads one and matched in the engine, of which a link must match one when there are any, besides `crawl.scope.strategy`, which they never replace. None by default. Fixed for a Run's life.

strategy.description: What a crawl's links are measured by against every seed, on every enqueue, redirect and Hook rewrite: `same_hostname` (Crawlee's default), `same_domain` (the registrable domain under the Public Suffix List), `same_origin` or `all`. One leading `www.` label is ignored, and under `same_origin` an `http` seed also admits its host's `https` origin on the same port. A link outside it is not added with `out_of_scope`. Fixed for a Run's life.

address.description: Where `daemon run`, the foreground Daemon, listens, as `host:port`: `127.0.0.1` on port 7900 plus the major (7600 plus the minor during `0.y` previews). Port 0 takes a free port, which its log names. Only a loopback address, until the Daemon terminates TLS. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy, or for `daemon run` through `GOODFETCH_DAEMON_ADDRESS`.

drain_grace.description: How long `daemon run`, the foreground Daemon, drains on `SIGTERM` before it exits: 110 seconds, below the 120-second `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` of the Helm chart, which must exceed it. Each run that reaches its next safe point in that time stops with a Checkpoint, resumable by its Run ID; one that does not stays resumable from its run file. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy, or for `daemon run` through `GOODFETCH_DAEMON_DRAIN_GRACE` in milliseconds.

idle_timeout.description: How long a Daemon with no connected Client, a visible Console tab included, waits before it stops: 10 minutes. `daemon start --keep-alive`, a held Schedule and an installed service keep it running. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

max_rows.description: The most rows one `dataset.query` returns; the rest are counted in its `total`, not returned. 10,000 by default.

memory_limit.description: The most memory, in bytes, one `dataset.query` may use; past it, the query fails with `query_memory_exceeded`. 512 MiB (536870912) by default.

report_guarantee_class.description: Every delivery reports its Guarantee class, an honesty guarantee that stays locked whatever the layer.

write_ids_and_epochs.description: Every write a Sink makes carries its delivery ID and run epoch, an honesty guarantee that stays locked whatever the layer.

allowed_domains.description: The hosts a run's requests may reach: each entry its host and their subdomains, matched on the host as a browser's URL parser leaves it (punycode, dotted-decimal IPv4), and `*` every host, only when written. `["*"]` by default; set for a connection or a Run, and only narrowed by a Recipe or a Client acting for a model, whose value listing a host the value below does not cover is `setting_locked`. A request to a host it does not list fails with `egress_refused`.

blocked_domains.description: The hosts no request of a run may reach, whatever `egress.allowed_domains` allows: each entry its host and their subdomains, matched as `egress.allowed_domains` matches, and `*` every host. Empty by default; set for a connection or a Run, and only added to by a Recipe or a Client acting for a model, whose value that leaves a host the value below lists uncovered is `setting_locked`. A request to a host it lists fails with `egress_refused`.

oneOf.description: An interface's name, such as `eth0`, or an IPv6 prefix, such as `2001:db8:1::/48`.

local_addresses.description: The addresses a Session's connections and DNS queries leave from (ADR 0044): a list of the host's IP addresses, such as `["192.0.2.10", "2001:db8::10"]`, a network interface's name, such as `eth0`, whose addresses are read when each Session starts, or an IPv6 prefix, such as `2001:db8:1::/48`. Each Session binds one address of each IP family for its life, new Sessions spread round-robin across the blocks `egress.rotation_block.ipv4` and `.ipv6` size. A prefix covers the host's addresses inside it, and on Linux any address of it once `net.ipv6.ip_nonlocal_bind` is 1 and the prefix is routed locally. A value that yields no address the host can use refuses the run with `local_address_unavailable`, and a site with no address in a family the Session holds fails with `address_family_unavailable`. None by default: the address the OS chooses. A Recipe may expose it but never sets it, since its addresses are the machine's own.

no_private_endpoints.description: Whether Operator-configured endpoints (Model providers, Secret providers, proxies, Notification webhooks, OTLP collectors, the Plugin index, a configured `cdp_url`) are refused every address that is not globally reachable, as the addresses a page can reach are, so a tenant's endpoint never reaches the network the engine runs in. `false` by default, so an endpoint on localhost or a private network works; set only in an Operator policy, as Goodfetch Cloud sets it. A refused endpoint fails with `egress_refused` before it connects.

offline.description: Whether the engine opens no connection nobody configured: every pinned download, such as a Pinned artifact missing from the Browser cache, fails with `artifact_unavailable_offline` before it connects, naming the command that supplies it beforehand. `false` by default; set at every layer, and an Operator policy can lock it.

private_ranges.description: The ranges and hosts that addresses a page can reach may use although they are not globally reachable, for tests against a local site or an intranet: CIDR ranges such as `127.0.0.0/8`, IP addresses, and host names, each name's connections allowed any address that is not globally reachable. A cloud-metadata address (`169.254.169.254`, `fd00:ec2::254`, `100.100.100.200`) is reached only when listed by its exact address, never through a range or a host name that covers it. Empty by default; set by the program's own code, configuration or an Operator policy, by a Recipe only where the Operator policy's `egress.recipe_private_ranges` allows it, and never by a Client acting for a model, whose value is `setting_locked`. A run that lists any records it once in the Audit log as `private_addresses_allowed` and in its Run report's `weakened`.

items.description: A CIDR range such as `127.0.0.0/8`, an IP address such as `169.254.169.254`, or a host name such as `intranet.example`.

recipe_private_ranges.description: Whether a Recipe may set `egress.private_ranges`. `false` by default, so a Recipe's value is `setting_locked`; set only in an Operator policy.

ipv4.description: The prefix length of the IPv4 blocks new Sessions are spread across, round-robin, when `egress.local_addresses` gives several: 24 by default, so consecutive Sessions leave from different /24 networks while the addresses allow it. Set for a connection or a Run.

ipv6.description: The prefix length of the IPv6 blocks new Sessions are spread across, round-robin, when `egress.local_addresses` gives several: 64 by default, the block a rate limiter such as Cloudflare's counts as one client. Set for a connection or a Run.

bom.description: Whether a CSV Export starts with a UTF-8 byte order mark, which some spreadsheet programs need to read it as UTF-8 and which Python's `csv` module, Node's csv-parse and Unix tools read as part of the first column's name: off by default. Set for the connection or the Run.

delimiter.description: The one character between a CSV Export's fields: `,` by default, or such as `;` or a tab. A double quote, a carriage return, a line feed, or a text of more or less than one character fails the Export with `setting_invalid`. Set for the connection or the Run.

nested.description: How a CSV Export writes a field whose value is an object: `json`, the default, its JSON text in the field's column; `flatten`, each of its fields in a column of its own named by its dotted path, such as `author.name`, at any depth. An array, and an empty object, is its JSON text either way. Set for the connection or the Run.

link.description: The field of each Record that an RSS item's or an Atom entry's link is taken from: `url` by default; it is also the entry's ID in Atom and the item's `guid` in RSS. A Record without it gets no link, and in Atom an ID from the Run, the Dataset and its number. An empty text fails the Export with `setting_invalid`. Set for the connection or the Run.

published.description: The field of each Record that an RSS item's `pubDate` and an Atom entry's `published` and `updated` are taken from: `published` by default, read as an RFC 3339 or RFC 2822 date and time. A Record without it, or whose value is no such date, gets no date in RSS, and in Atom the time it was committed as `updated`. An empty text fails the Export with `setting_invalid`. Set for the connection or the Run.

summary.description: The field of each Record that an RSS item's `description` and an Atom entry's `summary` are taken from, as text: `summary` by default. A Record without it gets none. An empty text fails the Export with `setting_invalid`. Set for the connection or the Run.

title.description: The field of each Record that an RSS item's or an Atom entry's title is taken from: `title` by default. A Record without it gets an empty title, or in RSS none where it has a summary. An empty text fails the Export with `setting_invalid`. Set for the connection or the Run.

indent.description: How many spaces a JSON Export indents each level by: 0, the default, writes the array and each Record's value on one line, as committed; 1 to 8 write the array one value per line and each value's members on lines of their own, indented by that many spaces per level. JSONL is one line per Record either way. A count above 8 fails the Export with `setting_invalid`. Set for the connection or the Run.

compression.description: The codec a Parquet Export compresses each column's pages with: `zstd`, the default, `snappy`, or `none`. It is inside the file, which every Parquet reader decodes, apart from the Export's own `compression`. Set for the connection or the Run.

sheet.description: The name of an XLSX Export's one sheet: none by default, which names it after the Dataset, each character a sheet name cannot hold (`:`, `\`, `/`, `?`, `*`, `[` and `]`) written as `_` and cut to 31 characters. A name that is empty, longer than 31 characters, holds one of those characters, or starts or ends with `'` fails the Export with `setting_invalid`. Set for the connection or the Run.

record.description: The name of the element an XML Export writes each Record in: `record` by default. A text that is no XML name without a colon (a letter or `_`, then letters, digits, `-`, `.` and `_`) fails the Export with `setting_invalid`. Set for the connection or the Run.

root.description: The name of an XML Export's root element, which holds one element per Record: `records` by default. A text that is no XML name without a colon (a letter or `_`, then letters, digits, `-`, `.` and `_`) fails the Export with `setting_invalid`. Set for the connection or the Run.

coalesce.description: Whether identical GET or HEAD crawl requests in flight at once from one Session, from work items that declare no Effect, wait for one response: the same method, URL, headers and body. Never across Sessions or runs, never for a Paid fetch; Provenance records each response shared. On by default.

encoding.description: The encoding forced on each crawl request's own document after its BOM, a WHATWG Encoding label such as `shift_jis`, set for the Run or for one of its Labels; none by default. It stands where ADR 0119's order puts it: after the BOM, before the `Content-Type` charset, the `<meta>` prescan and UTF-8. It applies to the request's own document on every attempt, not to a handler's own navigations. A value that is no Encoding label is refused with `setting_invalid` when the crawl starts.

enabled.description: Whether the HTTP tier hedges a crawl request: once a GET or HEAD from a work item that declares no Effect has not answered within its route's 95th-percentile latency, a second copy is sent on a new connection through the Session's own exit, and the first answer wins, the other cancelled. Both copies hold per-domain slots and count in Usage; a Paid fetch is never hedged. Off by default; a crawl that switches it on while `politeness.domain.concurrency` is 1 is refused with `setting_not_applicable`.

max_percent.description: The most hedges a run sends, as a whole percentage of the crawl requests its HTTP tier sent: 5 by default.

urls.description: URL patterns, each a glob or a regular expression matched in the engine, naming the responses of a crawl request's own navigation kept for its handler's `keptResponse` and `keptResponses`, set for the Run or for one of its Labels, whose own list wins for its requests. None by default: nothing is kept. Only a tier that runs the page's scripts, or `discovered_api`, can keep them: forcing `http` or `browser_fetch` where a list is set fails the crawl's start with `setting_not_applicable`; any other list set is refused at the start with `capability_unavailable` until the engine keeps responses.

light_browser.description: Whether a crawl may fetch on the `light_browser` tier: Lightpanda, run out of process, its build downloaded on first use into the Browser cache with its pinned digest and never bundled, so its AGPL licence stays outside the distribution. It runs the page's scripts without layout, and its page is the document they leave, so a wait for scripted content is served from it while a call that needs layout, pixels, a script of the handler's or a navigation escalates under `auto` and fails with `browser_required` under a forced tier. Set for the Run only. Off by default: `fetch.tier: light_browser` then fails the crawl's start with `capability_unavailable` naming this key, as it does on a platform Lightpanda builds nothing for.

max.description: How many redirects a crawl request's fetch follows, a refresh stub's hop counted as one: 19 by default, as many as the browser follows in a navigation, from 1 to 19; any other value is refused with `setting_invalid` when the crawl starts. One more fails the request with `too_many_redirects`, so a redirect loop costs a site this many requests and one more. To hand a redirect to the handler unfollowed, list its status in `crawl.handle_statuses`.

max_delay.description: The longest delay of a refresh stub a crawl request's fetch follows: a `Refresh` header, or a `<meta http-equiv="refresh">` outside `<noscript>`, to another URL with a delay up to this is followed at once as one more hop, counted in `fetch.redirect.max`. 100 s by default; `0` follows instant refreshes only, and `null` any delay. A refresh with no URL or to the document's own is never followed.

count.description: How many of a Label's first requests on a domain are samples under `fetch.tier: auto`, each fetched on `http` and then on `browser`, whose run commits: the Label moves to `http` once all of them gave the same Records and enqueues. 3 by default; set for the Run only. Fewer than 3 is a weakened control, named in the Run report's `weakened`.

refresh_after.description: When a Label's tier choice on a domain under `fetch.tier: auto` is sampled again: after it served `requests` crawl requests, or `after` milliseconds after it was made, whichever comes first; 500 requests or 24 hours (86,400,000 ms) by default. Set for the Run only. A Label whose browser sample showed a consent wall stays on `browser` and is not sampled again.

after.description: The milliseconds a Label's tier choice on a domain stands before it is sampled again.

requests.description: The requests a Label's tier choice on a domain serves before it is sampled again.

tier.description: The tier that fetches each crawl request's document, set for the Run or for one of its Labels: `auto` (the default) lets the engine choose: set for the Run or a Label, it learns the tier per Label on each domain by sample comparison, the first `fetch.sample.count` requests (3) of a Label on a domain each run on `http` and then on `browser`, whose run commits, the Label moving to `http` once all of them staged the same Records (compared after Unicode NFC and whitespace normalization of their strings, in any order) and the same enqueues, the browser's run never matching where it ended on another URL or read its document in another `document.characterSet`, and staying on `browser` for the Run where its browser sample met a consent wall; split by the first segment of its URL paths when its samples disagree by segment (a segment whose own samples disagree stays on `browser`; at most 16 segments per Label and domain, the rest on `browser`), and on `browser` otherwise; a choice is sampled again as `fetch.sample.refresh_after` says; the choice is kept in the run file, so a resumed crawl takes it again, and Provenance records each attempt's tier and whether it was forced; a request on `http` escalates to the browser at the first call that tier cannot serve exactly; left at the built-in default it still gives the handler its request alone; `http` and `browser` force those tiers, nothing escalating, and a call the forced tier cannot serve fails with `browser_required`; `light_browser` forces the Lightpanda tier where `fetch.light_browser` allows it, and under `auto` a Run that allows it also runs a sample on `light_browser` where its `http` run differed, the Label moving to `light_browser` once every sample matched there or over `http`; under `auto`, a sample whose `http` run escalated at a network wait also runs on `discovered_api` once its browser run answered: the JSON calls the browser's page made, read as a page-number or cursor plan, are replayed over HTTP for the same request, a `page.wait_for_response` armed before a navigation of its page answered from the calls that navigation replays and any other escalating, and a Label whose samples all matched there, or over `http`, moves to `discovered_api`, its later requests replaying the plan for their own pages; `browser_fetch` forces the HTTP tier sent from inside the Session's browser context, its TLS fingerprint and cookies the Session's, nothing escalating; forcing `discovered_api` is refused with `capability_unavailable` at the crawl's start until a forced tier takes its browser sample.

tier_race.description: Whether a crawl request races its tiers: browser-fetch first, then the navigation after the Label-on-domain's median browser-fetch latency, the first result that passes the Page check and the Label's comparison winning, both counting in Politeness and Usage. The loser is cancelled, and Provenance records the race. Set for the Run only: a Label setting it is refused with `setting_not_applicable`, as is a Run switching it on while `politeness.domain.concurrency` is 1, where the navigation could never start. Off by default.

ads.description: Whether a browser Session blocks ads by EasyList, as a blocker does: on by default in every Access mode. A blocked request fails as `BlockedByClient`; the never-block list keeps challenge, anti-bot, anti-fraud and payment scripts loading.

annoyances.description: Whether a browser Session blocks page annoyances (social widgets, newsletter and notification prompts) by Fanboy Annoyance, its cookie sections left to the Consent prompt runner: on by default in every Access mode.

extra.description: Extra Filter lists, by URL or path. Their scriptlets run only when the value comes from an Operator policy or user or project configuration; from a Recipe or a run, only their blocking rules apply.

first_party_scripts.description: Whether a site's own scripts load whatever the Filter lists say: off by default.

page_scriptlets.description: Whether the Filter lists' scriptlets that patch a page's JavaScript run, from uBlock Origin's resources downloaded with the lists that name them: off by default, since a site can see them.

trackers.description: Whether a browser Session blocks trackers by EasyPrivacy: on by default in every Access mode. A blocked request fails as `BlockedByClient`; the never-block list keeps challenge, anti-bot, anti-fraud and payment scripts loading.

contexts_per_process.description: How many of a Run's Sessions share one browser process, each in a browser context of its own: 8. The Run's next Session past it gets a process of its own; Sessions of different Runs never share one.

memory_cap.description: The memory, in bytes, of a browser and its processes past which it is recycled; unset by default, when the cap is twice what the browser used once it had opened its first page.

page_memory_cap.description: The memory, in bytes, of one page's JavaScript heap and the buffers it holds, past which the Resource governor ends the page while memory is critical: 1 GiB. The page ends at its safe point, once no call on it is in flight, and its calls raise `page_memory_exceeded`, which is retryable.

recycle_idle.description: How long a browser may hold no open page before it closes, each of its Sessions keeping its cookies and storage for the browser that replaces it: 5 minutes.

recycle_pages.description: How many pages a browser opens before it is recycled: 100. Recycled, it opens no new page, closes once its pages are done and is replaced, each of its Sessions keeping its cookies and storage.

ceiling.description: The most browser pages the engine's Resource governor admits open at once, across its Runs: 32.

floor.description: The fewest browser pages the engine's Resource governor keeps admitting at once, however loaded the machine: 1. Equal to `governor.browser_page.ceiling`, it fixes the concurrency there.

critical.description: The share of the Memory allowance in use, in percent, from which the engine's memory is critical: 95.

ceiling.description: The most HTTP and discovered-API fetches the engine's Resource governor admits at once, across its Runs: 200.

floor.description: The fewest HTTP and discovered-API fetches the engine's Resource governor keeps admitting at once, however loaded the machine: 1. Equal to `governor.http.ceiling`, it fixes the concurrency there.

last_resort_after.description: How long the engine's memory may stay critical with its concurrency at the floor before the Resource governor reaches its last resort, when a Daemon's `/readyz` fails: 60 s.

memory_allowance.description: The most memory, in bytes, the engine and its children may use, as its Memory allowance when it is tighter than the process's own cgroup limit, its Windows Job object's limit or half of physical memory; unset by default. Read again at every sample.

ceiling.description: The most model calls the engine's Resource governor admits at once, across its Runs: 16.

floor.description: The fewest model calls the engine's Resource governor keeps admitting at once, however loaded the machine: 1. Equal to `governor.model_call.ceiling`, it fixes the concurrency there.

pressure.description: The share of the Memory allowance in use, in percent, from which the engine is under pressure and its Resource governor lowers its concurrency; also the CPU and Tokio workers' busy share from which they hold it: 85.

run_share.description: The share, in percent, of each kind's concurrency one Run may hold at once, at least one: 100. An Operator policy cap bounds every Run's share.

sample_interval.description: How often the engine's Resource governor reads memory, CPU and Tokio saturation, sizes its concurrency and sends `engine.system_info`: every second.

hiding.description: Whether a Session's pages hide, on the live page, the elements the Filter lists' cosmetic rules match: `auto` (the default) and `always` hide them through a style sheet the site cannot see on Chromium, in every frame and every new document; `off` leaves the live page as served. When the guard finds an action's target hidden, it lifts the rule for the Session and acts. Extracted content has the elements removed whatever this says.

max_files.description: How many log files an engine process keeps where `log.output` is `file`, the one it writes included: 5, so a Daemon's logs stay under about 50 MiB. The oldest goes at each rotation. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

max_size.description: The size, in bytes, at which an engine process's log file rotates where `log.output` is `file`: 10 MiB. A file holds at most this much and one line more. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

format.description: How an engine process writes its logs on stderr, or on stdout under `daemon run`: `text`, lines for a person reading a terminal, or `json`, JSON lines. Unset, the logs are text on stderr and JSON lines on stdout under `daemon run`; a log file holds JSON lines whatever it says. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

level.description: Which of its logs an engine process writes: `info`, the default, which logs state changes only (a Run started, resumed or stopped, a domain backing off, a storage level changing, a Daemon draining) and never one line per request, or any `tracing` filter directive, such as `warn` or `info,goodfetch::rpc=debug`. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

output.description: Where an engine process writes its logs beside stderr: `stdout`, JSON lines for the platform to collect and rotate, `file`, JSON lines in its own files of the Goodfetch home's log folder, rotated at `log.file.max_size` and kept to `log.file.max_files`, or `none`. Unset, it is `stdout` under `daemon run`, `file` for every other Daemon and `none` for an Attached engine, whose logs go to its Client as log events; `stdout` on an Attached engine, whose stdout is its protocol, fails with `setting_not_applicable`. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

max_body_size.description: The most decoded bytes of one body the engine itself reads: a page `request`'s response, a kept response, an Operator-configured endpoint's reply. Never a download, which the disk governor bounds. 64 MiB (67108864) by default; set for a connection or a Run. A longer body fails the call with `response_limit_exceeded`.

max_decompression_ratio.description: The most decoded bytes per received byte of a body the engine reads, once its decoded bytes pass 1 MiB, so a decompression bomb is stopped as it expands. 100 by default; set for a connection or a Run. A body past it fails the call with `response_limit_exceeded`.

max_json_depth.description: The deepest nesting of arrays and objects in JSON the engine parses from outside, from 0 to 1024: 128 by default; set for a connection or a Run. Deeper JSON fails the call with `response_limit_exceeded`.

resolve.description: Host names mapped to addresses before any lookup, in the engine's resolver and in Chromium, each address still checked by ADR 0017's resolved-address rule. Empty by default; an Operator policy can lock it.

address.description: Where `daemon run`, the foreground Daemon, serves its ops listener, as `host:port`: `/livez` and `/readyz` answer a status and no body to anyone, and `/metrics`, Prometheus' text, only with the ops token, the `ops.token` file of the major's folder, as a bearer token. Unset by default: no ops listener and no Prometheus export. Any address, so a cluster's probes and scrapers reach it; a request whose `Host` is a name other than `localhost`, or that carries an `Origin`, is refused. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy, or for `daemon run` through `GOODFETCH_OPS_ADDRESS`.

logs_endpoint.description: The OTLP/HTTP endpoint an engine process sends its OpenTelemetry events to, such as `http://localhost:4318/v1/logs`: today the Audit log's entries, while `audit.otlp` is on. Unset, the default, sends nothing, and nothing leaves the machine. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

metrics_endpoint.description: The OTLP/HTTP endpoint `daemon run`, the foreground Daemon, exports its metrics to, in protobuf, every 60 seconds and once more as it exits: a full URL such as `http://collector:4318/v1/metrics`. Unset by default: nothing is exported (ADR 0043).

traces_endpoint.description: The OTLP/HTTP endpoint an engine process exports its `tracing` spans to, such as `http://localhost:4318/v1/traces`; unset, the default, exports nothing, and nothing leaves the machine. The spans cover each run, page and CDP command, with glossary IDs and bounded values as fields and a URL as its origin. Span names, span fields and the engine's targets are Experimental: a minor may change them, and its release notes list the change. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

chain_rpc_endpoints.description: The RPC endpoint of each chain whose finalized state proves a payment did not settle, by chain. Set only in an Operator policy and user and project configuration.

domains.description: The registrable domains a run may pay for a page; `*` only when written. Widened only in an Operator policy, user or project configuration, or by a person's answer; a Recipe or a run only narrows it.

exchange_rates.description: The fixed rates that convert a price into a Limit's currency, by currency pair. Set only in an Operator policy and user and project configuration.

max_price_per_page.description: The most a run pays for one page, as an amount and its currency such as `0.05 USD`; none by default. Raised only in configuration; a Recipe or a run only lowers it.

enabled.description: Whether a domain that answers 429, 502, 503 or 504, or does not answer in time, is backed off, and its `Retry-After` waited out, for every run of the user that shares Politeness. Off, the run ignores both, and it is listed in the run's result.

initial.description: The shortest wait of a domain's backoff: each wait is drawn at random between it and three times the previous wait (the first between it and three times it), never above `politeness.backoff.max`: 2 s. A shorter value is listed in the run's result.

max.description: The longest wait of a domain's backoff: 60 s. A `Retry-After` may hold the domain longer, up to `politeness.retry_after.max`. A shorter value is listed in the run's result.

adaptive_delay.description: Whether a domain key's delay between request starts lengthens as its responses slow: on, the delay is the longer of `politeness.domain.delay` and the exponentially weighted mean (weight 0.3) of the latency of its last responses on the `http` tier, that mean capped at `politeness.backoff.max`. It only lengthens the delay, never below `politeness.domain.delay`. Off by default.

burst.description: How many crawl requests may start at once on one domain key under `politeness.domain.rate`, the size of its token bucket: 1 by default, so the starts are spread evenly over the minute. A value of 0 is read as 1.

concurrency.description: How many requests may be in flight at once on one domain key, counted across every run of the user that shares Politeness: a run admits one only while that combined count is below its own value. None by default until the fetch tiers set ADR 0086's default of 1. A value above 1 is listed in the run's result as one that presses a site harder.

delay.description: How long a run waits after the last request start on a domain key, by any run of the user that shares Politeness, before it starts another there. None by default until the fetch tiers set ADR 0086's default of 1 s. A value below 1 s is listed in the run's result as one that presses a site harder.

rate.description: How many crawl requests a minute may start on one domain key, counted across every run of the user that shares Politeness, as a token bucket of `politeness.domain.burst` tokens refilled at this rate: 30 holds a site to 30 requests a minute. Each run is held to its own value; the delay between starts still applies. None by default.

concurrency.description: How many page navigations may be in flight at once through one proxy endpoint and credential, counted across every run of the user that shares Politeness, each redirect hop of a page's main frame counted, a program's own navigation included (a page's other requests and `page.request` are not counted): a run sends one only while that combined count is below its own value and below the ceiling the proxy's own refusals taught. At least 1; none by default, for no cap.

rate.description: How many page navigations a second may start through one proxy endpoint and credential, counted across every run of the user that shares Politeness, each redirect hop of a page's main frame counted, a program's own navigation included (a page's other requests and `page.request` are not counted): a run starts one only once a second divided by its own value has passed since the last start there by any sharing run. None by default.

max.description: The longest a crawl waits for the time a site's `Retry-After` asks, past `politeness.backoff.max`: 15 minutes. When the site asks for longer, nothing is sent to its domain before that time and nothing waits for it: the request whose response asked, and each request admitted to the domain meanwhile, ends `failed` with `response_unavailable`, and `run.retry_failed` re-admits them once the site is back. Whatever its value, nothing is sent sooner than the site asked.

sharing.description: How a Run shares Politeness with the other runs of its user: `shared` with every engine of the user (through the Politeness store when one is configured, else on the machine), `per_daemon` on the machine only, ignoring a store, or `run` for Politeness of its own. Anything but `shared` is listed in the Run's result.

bypass.description: The hosts the Session reaches without its proxy, as Playwright's `bypass`: a comma-separated list such as `.example.com, chromium.org`, a leading dot naming a domain's subdomains. None by default: every request goes through `proxy.server`. Set as `proxy.server` is.

anyOf.description: An ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, such as `US`.

country.description: The country, an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code such as `US`, a Session's proxy exit is in. None by default: any country the provider offers. A country the provider does not offer for the Session's proxy kind is refused with `setting_invalid` when the Session opens. A Recipe never sets it (`setting_locked`).

kind.description: The proxy kind a Session's proxy is drawn from, `datacenter`, `isp`, `residential` or `mobile`: the provider's default when unset, for `list` the kind of its first server. A kind the provider does not offer is refused with `setting_invalid` when the Session opens. A Recipe may set it.

password.description: The Secret reference of the password the Session gives `proxy.server` with `proxy.username`, such as `env:PROXY_PASSWORD`: never a value, resolved when the Session opens and never written to a log, a trace, a process's arguments or a file. None by default. Set as `proxy.server` is.

provider.description: The Proxy provider each Session of the Run, or the Session it is set on, draws its one proxy from when it opens, fixed for the Session's life: `bright_data`, `oxylabs` or `apify`, whose adapters build the provider's sticky-session username from the account in `proxy.providers.<name>` and ask for the provider's longest sticky lifetime, or `list`, the user's own servers in `proxy.providers.list.servers`. None by default. A Session that resolves both `proxy.server` and `proxy.provider` is refused with `setting_invalid`. Set as `proxy.server` is: a Recipe may expose it but never sets it, and a Client acting for a model is refused with `setting_locked`.

password.description: The Secret reference of the account's password, such as `env:PROXY_PASSWORD`.

price.description: The price of a GB (10^9 bytes) through it, as an amount and its currency.

servers.description: The user's own servers, for `list` only.

providers.description: What each Proxy provider takes, by name, such as `proxy.providers.list`: `username`, the account's; `password`, a Secret reference resolved when a Session opens; `endpoint`, the provider's proxy URL in place of its public one (`http://brd.superproxy.io:33335` for `bright_data`, `http://pr.oxylabs.io:7777` for `oxylabs`, `http://proxy.apify.com:8000` for `apify`), an `http://`, `socks5://` or `socks5h://` URL, never `https://`, which the Session's loopback relay speaks no TLS to; `servers`, for `list` only, the user's own proxies, each a table of `server` (an `http://`, `socks5://` or `socks5h://` URL), `kind` and an optional `country`; and `price`, the price of a GB (10^9 bytes) through the provider, such as `5 USD`, which a currency Limit on `proxy_bytes` charges: under such a Limit a Session of an unpriced provider, or one priced in another currency, is refused with `setting_invalid`. Empty by default. Set only in an Operator policy and user and project configuration: a Recipe's or a run's value is `setting_locked`, so no Client lowers a price.

anyOf.description: A proxy URL, `http://`, `https://`, `socks5://` or `socks5h://`, with a host and an optional port and never credentials, such as `http://proxy.example:3128`.

server.description: The proxy every request of the Session goes through, as Playwright's `server`: an `http://`, `https://`, `socks5://` or `socks5h://` URL with a host and a port, such as `http://proxy.example:3128`. None by default: the machine's own address. Set on a Run, every Session of it takes it; set in `run.new_session`'s `settings`, that Session alone; a page or a request has no proxy of its own, so the address a site sees never changes under the same cookies. A URL carrying credentials and `socks4` are refused with `setting_invalid`: give the credentials as `proxy.username` and `proxy.password`. Set only by the program's own code, configuration and an Operator policy: a Recipe may expose it but never sets it, and a Client acting for a model is refused with `setting_locked`, since whoever sets it receives `proxy.password`. On Chromium, a SOCKS5 proxy's credentials go through a loopback relay the engine opens for the Session.

sticky_lifetime.description: How long, in milliseconds, a Session asks its provider to keep its proxy exit: the provider's longest when unset. A Session that outlives it is named by the Run report's `proxy_exit_may_change` warning; the engine never looks the exit up. A `list` server's exit never changes.

username.description: The username the Session gives `proxy.server`, as Playwright's `username`. None by default. Set as `proxy.server` is.

attempt_delay.description: How long the engine's HTTP transports let a connection attempt to one of a host's addresses run before they start the next one beside it: 250 ms, RFC 8305's Connection Attempt Delay. An attempt that fails starts the next at once.

resolution_delay.description: How long the engine's HTTP transports wait for a host's IPv6 addresses once its IPv4 addresses arrived first, before they start connecting over IPv4: 50 ms, RFC 8305's Resolution Delay.

durability.description: How a Run's commits reach the disk: `full`, the default, keeps every acknowledged commit through a power cut (`synchronous=FULL`, with `fullfsync` on macOS); `fast` (`synchronous=NORMAL`) survives a process crash only, since an OS crash or a power cut may roll back recent commits, possibly many, without damaging the run state. A Run in `fast` names it in its run report's `weakened`.

key_reference.description: The Secret reference of the key-encryption key that wraps each Run's data key. One set in a layer is resolved when a Run starts: a Run whose reference does not resolve is refused with `secret_unavailable`. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration. By default the OS keychain's `keychain:goodfetch/run-state-key`, or, on a host with no OS keychain, the encrypted local file's `secretfile:run-state-key`, which `config explain` shows as the default it chose; the engine makes the default's item, a random 256-bit key, where it is missing when a Run first seals a field. A Run's data key is stored only wrapped by this key, so a resume, such as of a Checkpoint moved to another machine, unwraps it with the key this setting names for the resume, which a Client may send in `run.resume`'s project configuration: one that gives no value fails the resume with `secret_unavailable`, one that does not open the data key with `run_key_mismatch`. The encrypted local file, `secrets/<name>.age` in Goodfetch home encrypted with age to the X25519 identity in `secrets/identity.txt`, a file only its owner may read, protects copies and backups of the home, not the value from another process of the same user.

layout.description: Where Runs keep their run state: `per_run`, the default, one SQLite file in each run folder; `per_install`, one database, `run-state.sqlite` in the per-major folder, holding every Run of the install and major and written by the Daemon alone, to which an Attached engine then hands its Runs. Export, import and Checkpoint give the same per-run file in both. Taken only from the machine's own layers, and read when the Daemon starts.

location.description: The folder that holds the run folders, each named by its Run ID; by default the per-user, per-major data folder of the Goodfetch home.

echo_repeats.description: How many times the sample operation repeats a text.

endpoint.description: The URL of the Secrets Manager endpoint that answers `aws-sm:` Secret references, such as a VPC endpoint's: unset, the default, the Region's public endpoint, `https://secretsmanager.<region>.amazonaws.com`. It is an Operator-configured endpoint: reached on a private address unless `egress.no_private_endpoints` refuses it, its certificate verified against Mozilla's roots and its own domain's `tls.trusted_cas`, never excepted by `tls.accept_invalid_certs`. Plain `http:` is taken only for a loopback address. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration.

region.description: The AWS Region, such as `eu-west-3`, whose Secrets Manager answers `aws-sm:name#key` Secret references: the engine calls `GetSecretValue` for the secret `name`, signed with the access key in its environment's `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` and, for temporary credentials, `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`, and answers the secret's text, or its JSON object's `key`. Unset, the default, the engine's environment's `AWS_REGION`, then `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`, names it; with none, an `aws-sm:` reference fails with `secret_unavailable`, `failure: "not_configured"`. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration.

authority.description: The URL of the Microsoft Entra ID authority that issues the access token `azure-kv:` references are read with, `https://login.microsoftonline.com` by default, or a sovereign cloud's, such as `https://login.chinacloudapi.cn`: the engine asks `<authority>/<AZURE_TENANT_ID>/oauth2/v2.0/token` for a token of the client-credentials grant. It is an Operator-configured endpoint, judged and verified as `secret_providers.azure_kv.endpoint` is. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration.

endpoint.description: The URL of the Azure Key Vault that answers `azure-kv:vault/secret` Secret references, `{vault}` standing for the reference's vault name: `https://{vault}.vault.azure.net` by default, or a sovereign cloud's, such as `https://{vault}.vault.azure.cn`. The engine reads the secret's current version with an access token for Key Vault that Microsoft Entra ID (`secret_providers.azure_kv.authority`) issues to the service principal in its environment's `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` and `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET`. With any of them unset, an `azure-kv:` reference fails with `secret_unavailable`, `failure: "not_configured"`. It is an Operator-configured endpoint: reached on a private address unless `egress.no_private_endpoints` refuses it, its certificate verified against Mozilla's roots and its own domain's `tls.trusted_cas`, never excepted by `tls.accept_invalid_certs`. Plain `http:` is taken only for a loopback address. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration.

command.description: The absolute path of the Bitwarden CLI, `bw`, that answers `bw:item/field` Secret references from Bitwarden or, once `bw config server` points it there, a Vaultwarden server: the engine runs `bw get` without interaction and with its own environment, so `BW_SESSION` unlocks the vault. `field` is `password`, `username`, `totp` (the current code, never the seed), `notes`, `uri` or the name of a custom field. Unset, the default, a `bw:` reference fails with `secret_unavailable`, `failure: "not_configured"`. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration.

endpoint.description: The URL of the Google Cloud Secret Manager API that answers `gcp-sm:project/secret/version` Secret references, `https://secretmanager.googleapis.com` by default, or a regional or Private Service Connect endpoint: the engine accesses the secret's version (`latest` for the newest) with the OAuth 2.0 access token in its environment's `GOOGLE_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN`, such as `gcloud auth print-access-token` prints, and answers its payload as text. With no token, a `gcp-sm:` reference fails with `secret_unavailable`, `failure: "not_configured"`. It is an Operator-configured endpoint: reached on a private address unless `egress.no_private_endpoints` refuses it, its certificate verified against Mozilla's roots and its own domain's `tls.trusted_cas`, never excepted by `tls.accept_invalid_certs`. Plain `http:` is taken only for a loopback address. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration.

command.description: The absolute path of the 1Password CLI, `op`, that answers `op://vault/item/field` Secret references: the engine runs `op read` with its own environment, so `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` or the desktop app's integration signs it in. Unset, the default, an `op://` reference fails with `secret_unavailable`, `failure: "not_configured"`. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration.

address.description: The URL of the HashiCorp Vault or OpenBao server that answers `vault:mount/path#field` Secret references, such as `https://vault.example.com:8200`: the engine reads `field` of the KV version 2 secret `path` in the secrets engine mounted at `mount`, with the token in its environment's `VAULT_TOKEN`, or `BAO_TOKEN`. It is an Operator-configured endpoint: reached on a private address unless `egress.no_private_endpoints` refuses it, its certificate verified against Mozilla's roots and its own domain's `tls.trusted_cas`, never excepted by `tls.accept_invalid_certs`. Plain `http:` is taken only for a loopback address, as a development server's. Unset, the default, a `vault:` reference fails with `secret_unavailable`, `failure: "not_configured"`. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration.

by_reference.description: Secrets are given by Secret reference, never as values, an honesty guarantee that stays locked whatever the layer.

resolve_each_use.description: The Secret references a Run resolves again at each use, such as a rotating token's. Any other reference is resolved once for each placeholder it fills and its value reused for the rest of the Run, its domain binding checked at each use; none by default.

audit_chain.description: Whether the run's Audit log entries are hash-chained (ADR 0016). On by default; off, that run's entries are written unchained, each marked `chained: false`, which `audit verify` steps over while it verifies the chain around them; the switch itself is a chained entry, and the run says so in its report's `weakened` and in one warning.

browser_sandbox.description: Whether Chromium's renderers run in their sandbox (ADRs 0017 and 0049): the engine never passes `--no-sandbox` while it is on. On by default, except on a host whose platform allows no sandbox (AWS Lambda, Fargate, Azure Container Apps), where the engine switches it off. Only an Operator policy or configuration switches it off; a Recipe's or a run's value is `setting_locked`. Off, the renderers run unsandboxed, and the run says so in its report's `weakened`, in the Audit log and in one warning.

field_encryption.description: Whether the run's state seals its secret fields with the run's data key (ADR 0015). On by default; off, they are written in the clear, and the run says so in its report's `weakened`, in the Audit log and in one warning.

raw_cdp_egress_proxy.description: Whether every browser Session the engine launches reaches the network through the egress relay, which holds a raw CDP client or a Lent page at the network layer (ADR 0017). On by default; off, a Session with no certificate exception and no local address connects directly, held by interception alone, and the run says so in its report's `weakened`, in the Audit log and in one warning. It never removes the relay that carries certificate exceptions or local addresses.

redaction.description: Whether logs, traces and HAR files are redacted and screenshots and recordings kept as outputs are masked (ADR 0014). On by default; off lifts that guarantee for those outputs only: secrets still never reach the model, Plans, caches, the Effect journal or observations. The run says so in its report's `weakened`, in the Audit log and in one warning.

resolved_ip_check.description: Whether every address a name resolves to is checked against the egress policy before a connection is made (ADR 0017). On by default; off, the domain policy alone applies, and the run says so in its report's `weakened`, in the Audit log and in one warning.

secure_delete.description: Whether the run's secret tables overwrite what they delete, SQLite's `secure_delete` (ADR 0015). On by default; off, deleted values may stay on disk until overwritten, and the run says so in its report's `weakened`, in the Audit log and in one warning.

anyOf.description:
What `session.page_check` holds (ADR 0092): the Session's login page
and its expected page, each optional. Without a login page no page is
judged a login page; without an expected page every other page passes.

One page match (ADR 0092), named by `kind`: the document's URL against
a glob or a regular expression, as `page.route` takes them (ADR 0081),
an element a CSS or `XPath` selector finds in it, or a text its body
shows.

oneOf.description: The document's URL matches a glob, as Playwright reads one.

The document's URL matches a regular expression, in the `regex`
crate's syntax, anywhere in it.
An element of the main frame's document matches a CSS selector.

An element of the main frame's document matches an `XPath`
expression.

The main frame's body shows a text, its runs of white space read as
one space, case and all.

expected_page.description: The page the Session's navigations should reach.

login_page.description:
The page a site shows instead of the expected page once the
Session's login is lost.

page_check.description: The Page check every page of a Session is judged against once its navigation reached its document: `login_page` and `expected_page`, each optional and each a page match, a URL glob or regular expression, a CSS or XPath selector, or a text. A page matching its login page raises `logged_out` from the call that waited for its navigation; one matching neither, when an expected page is given, raises `page_check_failed`. None by default: the built-in detector then judges a page a login page when the navigation was redirected to a login path, or when the page shows one password field outside a login path, and Provenance marks each page it judged as weakly checked. Set at a Run, a connection or a Session's own `settings`.

max_age.description: How long after it opened a Session of a crawl's Session pool is retired: 3,000 s, Crawlee's `maxAgeSecs`.

max_error_score.description: The error score at which a Session of a crawl's Session pool is retired: 3. A block or a failed Page check adds 1, a success takes 0.5 off, never below 0 (Crawlee's model).

max_size.description: How many Sessions a crawl's Session pool keeps open at once: 100. A request goes to a new Session while the pool has room, then to one drawn among those open.

max_uses.description: How many requests one Session of a crawl's Session pool serves before it is retired: 50, Crawlee's `maxUsageCount`.

anyOf.description: Where a Session's login comes from (ADR 0056): exactly one kind.

oneOf.description: A Saved identity, by its name.

A file of cookies and storage, read on the program's machine and
sent over the connection.

domains.description: The registrable domains its navigation is bound to.

anyOf.description: The format of a `state_file`, detected when left out.

oneOf.description: A session export bundle, opened with `key` (ADR 0015).

format.description: Its format, detected when left out.

key.description: The Secret reference that opens a session export bundle.

oneOf.description: A `Cookie` header's cookies, for one domain.
A Profile directory, used in place.

domains.description: The registrable domains its navigation is bound to.

oneOf.description: The data of a browser the person installed, read once.

domains.description: The registrable domains its data is read for.

oneOf.description: A browser the person runs, reached through its consented connection.

domains.description: The registrable domains its navigation is bound to.

oneOf.description: A browser at a CDP address (ADR 0115).

domains.description: The registrable domains its navigation is bound to.

exclusive.description: Whether nothing else drives the browser (ADR 0114).

headers.description: Headers its connection sends, each value a Secret reference.

source.description: Where a Session's login comes from: exactly one kind of ADR 0056's tagged union, or none for a fresh Session. Set at a Run or a connection, it is the default of the Sessions opened beneath; opening a Session takes its own as the call's `source`, and in that Session's own `settings` it is refused with `setting_not_applicable`. A Recipe never sets or locks it; it may only expose it to its users.

max_crawl_delay.description: The longest robots.txt Crawl-delay a crawl waits out between request starts on a domain key while `site_preferences.respect_robots_txt` is on: 30 s. A host asking for more has its crawl requests skipped with `crawl_delay`, and its delay is not raised.

purpose.description: What the run's results are for, against which the AI-use signals are judged while `site_preferences.respect_use_signals` is on: `search` (the default, which no signal is judged against), `ai-input` (input to an AI model), `ai-train` (training an AI model) or `collect` (plain collection, text and data mining).

respect_robots_txt.description: Whether every crawl request, start URLs and sitemap entries included, and every navigation a handler makes, obeys the site's robots.txt (RFC 9309): a request it disallows, or one waiting on a robots.txt that answers 429 or 5xx or no answer, with no earlier copy, until its retries ran out, ends `skipped` with `robots_txt` and its handler never runs. On by default. Off, robots.txt is read but not obeyed, and it is listed in the run's result as a value that presses a site harder.

respect_use_signals.description: Whether the AI-use signals a site sends (IETF aipref's `Content-Usage` header, TDMRep's `tdm-reservation` header) are applied to the run's `site_preferences.purpose`: on, a crawl request whose response's signal refuses the Purpose ends `skipped` with `use_signals` and its handler never runs. Off by default; the signals are read either way.

robots_txt_user_agent.description: The operator's own robots.txt product token, letters, `_` and `-`: a crawl obeys the robots.txt groups naming it merged with those naming `goodfetch-foxhound`, each matched as a whole token in any case, and the `*` group only when neither has one. None by default. A value is listed in the run's result as one that presses a site harder.

critical_free.description: The free space, in bytes, below which a filesystem a Run writes to is at the `critical` storage level: every Run with an essential write on it stops resumably at its next safe point, with `resource: "storage"`, and a new Run whose run file would go there is refused with `resources_exhausted`. Unset, each filesystem takes the smaller of 1 GiB and 2 % of its size, and free inodes go by 2 %; `0` turns the level off, which the Run's report lists in `weakened`. Read again at every sample of the Resource governor; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

low_free.description: The free space, in bytes, below which a filesystem a Run writes to is at the `low` storage level: its Runs go on, record no Run trace video, store no new Response cache entry, skip their periodic Checkpoints onto it, and carry the warning `storage_low`. Unset, each filesystem takes the smaller of 5 GiB and 10 % of its size, and free inodes go by 10 %; `0` turns the level off, which the Run's report lists in `weakened`. Read again at every sample of the Resource governor; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

action.description: How long a locator action waits for its target to be unique and actionable, and replays a gesture that landed elsewhere, before it fails with `deadline_exceeded`, or `target_not_unique` for a target still ambiguous: 30 s.

close.description: How long a stop of a Run, `run.stop` or a scope's close, waits for its next safe point before it fails with `deadline_exceeded`, the Run still stopping there: 30 s.

dataset_query.description: How long one `dataset.query` may run before it is stopped and fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s.

first_byte.description: How long a request may wait for its response's first byte before its attempt fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s.

handler.description: How long a crawl's handler has for one attempt, which also bounds every action inside it, and from which a work item's lease is derived: the timeout plus the larger of 10 s and a tenth of it. 60 s, Crawlee's `requestHandlerTimeoutSecs`.

navigation.description: How long a navigation may take before its attempt fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s, Playwright's default.

run.description: How long a Run may go on before it checkpoints and stops at its next safe point, resumable; none by default.

secret.description: How long a Secret provider may take to answer one reference before the resolution fails with `secret_unavailable`, `failure: "timed_out"`: 30 s. A provider that answers it is briefly busy, such as a rate limit's, is asked again within it, with exponential backoff and full jitter, after its `Retry-After` when it gave one.

wait.description: How long a wait for an application state, such as `page.wait_for_request_finished`, may take before it fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s.

accept_invalid_certs.description: Domains whose certificate may fail verification, each with a pin, `any`, or `null` for trust on first use. A pin and `any` are taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration; a Recipe or a run may list a domain only for trust on first use.

certificate.description: The file of the client certificate and its chain, PEM or DER.

key.description: The Secret reference of the certificate's private key, such as `env:CLIENT_KEY`, resolved at the handshake.

client_certificates.description: Client certificates for mutual TLS by domain: a host or a registrable domain with its subdomains, mapped to a table of `certificate`, the file of the certificate and its chain (PEM or DER), and `key`, the Secret reference of its private key, such as `env:CLIENT_KEY`, resolved only when a handshake with a host of that domain starts; a key given as a value is refused with `setting_invalid`. The certificate goes to the domain's hosts and nowhere else, and never to a host reached through an exception of `tls.accept_invalid_certs`. Set from every layer, a Recipe and a run included; nothing is installed on the machine.

trusted_cas.description: Extra certificate authorities by domain: a host or a registrable domain with its subdomains, mapped to certificate files or Secret references, trusted beside the default roots for that domain and nowhere else. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration, never from a Recipe or a run; on a Daemon with accounts only the operator role writes it, in the Operator policy.

age_notice.description: Whether an executable more than three months past its release date prints one line a day on stderr saying so, from its own release date alone, with no network call. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

denied_domains.description: The domains whose Walls no run reads past, whatever another layer allows. Set only in an Operator policy.

domains.description: The domains whose Walls a run may read past by generic means. A Recipe or a run only narrows it; it is widened only in configuration or by a person's answer.

refetch_domains.description: The domains on which reading past a Wall may fetch a page again. A Recipe or a run only narrows it; it is widened only in configuration, never by an answer.

signing.description: Every webhook Goodfetch sends is signed, an honesty guarantee that stays locked whatever the layer.

version.description: The version of this format the file was written in.
